A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DC-LA research. Their text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–J support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix J report original synthetic sampling experiments, KL comparisons, and CT reconstruction and posterior-variance results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original synthetic and CT experiments and additionally reports a PSM PSNR trajectory in Figure 4.

M1.justification: DC-LA and DC-LA-S retain their smoothing, gradient, proximal, and noise-injection procedures. The CT proximal approximation is unchanged. New equivalent formulations and auxiliary proof constructions do not change the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two-dimensional synthetic distributions and Mayo CT reconstruction task, including the same additional covariance settings and CT scans in Appendix J. No dataset or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Synthetic comparisons retain ULA, Moreau ULA, and PSGLA; CT comparisons retain PSM MAP estimates at the same checkpoints. Newly cited sampling methods are not added to the empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported step sizes, smoothing parameters, chain counts and lengths, burn-in, acquisition geometry, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The new PSM trajectory reports progress within the existing 20,000-iteration optimization setting.

E4.justification: V2 adds Figure 4 to examine PSM reconstruction quality between 10,000 and 20,000 iterations, showing a peak followed by deterioration. The existing smoothing/step-size sensitivity study and single-chain versus multiple-chain diagnostics remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Chain counts and the pixel-wise posterior-variance reporting procedure are retained. V2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the comparisons.

E6.justification: Figure 3 changes DC-LA's reported PSNR from 26.2109 to 26.2303, while SSIM remains 0.8493. Figure 4 adds the PSM PSNR trajectory. Existing synthetic plots and appendix CT scores are retained; the PDFs do not establish that the revised score reflects a rerun or methodological improvement.

T1.justification: V1's brief small-lambda discussion in Appendix I.6 becomes a substantial parameter-dependence derivation in v2 Appendix I.7, supported by new zero-drift existence and Foster–Lyapunov lemmas. Appendix I.5 adds an auxiliary step size to justify uniform constants. New Appendices F.4–F.5 prove non-weak-convexity for PiL and the l1-minus-l2-power regularizer. The principal assumptions and convergence orders remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions narrow the CT claim from reliable uncertainty quantification to qualitatively reasonable uncertainty under the assumed model. The conclusion presents variance images as complementing MAP estimation rather than addressing a largely overlooked aspect. The central algorithmic and convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 clarifies that SSIM and PSNR measure reconstruction quality, not sampling accuracy, and explains computational costs when proximal maps lack closed forms. It adds discussion of the Lipschitz restriction on r1 and revises the PSM interpretation to distinguish improved endpoint performance from late overfitting.

D1.justification: The advertised code-repository path changes from MCS-hub/DC-LA26 to MCS-hub/DC-LA2026. New Remark 5.1 documents per-iteration gradient and proximal evaluation requirements. Existing hyperparameters, initialization, and proximal approximation details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Durmus et al. (2018), Habring et al. (2024, 2026), and Kuric et al. (2025), distinguishing related smoothing, subgradient, and Gibbs approaches. Laumont et al. (2022) and Teschl (2005) support new proofs. The central positioning beyond weakly convex regularizers remains.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language edits, adds explanatory remarks and disclosure statements, revises introductory and concluding passages, and swaps the order of the parameter-dependence and smoothing-bound appendices. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference main text with different typography, headers, and extensively resized and repositioned figures. Appendix illustrations are also redistributed. V2 adds the regularizer summary Table 1 and PSM trajectory Figure 4; the existing plotted and CT image content is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the existing theory more inspectable through expanded parameter derivations and supporting proofs. It also better qualifies the CT claims and supports the revised optimization interpretation with Figure 4. These improve transparency and interpretation, while the principal convergence results and empirical validation remain largely unchanged and the acknowledged CT applicability gaps persist.
